grammar.title: Cleft Sentences (It was... that, What I need is...)
grammar.explanation:
A **cleft sentence** splits one idea into two parts to **emphasise** one of them. It tells the listener exactly which part matters most.

**It-clefts** use **It is** or **It was**, then the focus, then **that** or **who**. Use **who** for people and **that** for things, places, or times.

**Wh-clefts** start with a **what** clause, then **is** or **was**, then the focus. For an action, use **do**: **What I did was** (to) + verb.

Keep the verb singular after **It** and after a **what** clause, even when the focus itself is plural.

Cleft sentences are also a polite way to correct someone. You can shift the focus, for example from money to people, without starting an argument.
examples: ***It was my sister who** told me the news.* (it-cleft, person)
***It's** the noise **that** I can't stand, not the heat.* (it-cleft, thing)
***It was** in Paris **that** they first met.* (it-cleft, place)
***What I need is** a long holiday.* (wh-cleft)
***What annoys me is** people who talk during films.* (wh-cleft)
***What we did was** book a taxi.* (wh-cleft, action)

practice.q: Rewrite with an it-cleft emphasising the APR: The APR worried the family most.
practice.a: It was the APR that worried the family most.

practice.q: Rewrite as a wh-cleft: We need more time to allocate funds fairly.
practice.a: What we need is more time to allocate funds fairly.

practice.q: Rewrite with an it-cleft emphasising last year: The council decided to allocate funds last year.
practice.a: It was last year that the council decided to allocate funds.

practice.q: Rewrite using 'What I did was': I checked the APR before signing the loan.
practice.a: What I did was check the APR before signing the loan.
